rationale: The workflow repeatedly fetches Go dependencies on every push run across three jobs (examples_go_py, deployments_k8s, deployments_k8s_network_emulation) and the repository pins go.mod/go.sum, satisfying the P-LIT-GHA-CACHE preconditions (repeated dependency fetching; cache inputs include lockfile and environment). No equivalent cache exists, and the module cache is trusted, input-keyed content, so there are no contraindications. The measured experiment (batch-interactive-three--f6d2974a5cef7cc9) showed adding actions/cache for ~/go/pkg/mod keyed on go.mod/go.sum reduced median elapsed time (~6%) while keeping all tests. I added a Cache Go modules step after Setup Go in each Go-using job, keyed on the repository's go.mod/go.sum, preserving every existing step, trigger, permission, and coverage. examples_curl uses neither Go nor Python, so it is left unchanged.
